figures.caption: Fig. 1. Comparison of representative SOTA dehazing methods on the Haze4K dataset. Left: MACs (G) vs. PSNR (dB); Right: Params (M) vs. PSNR (dB). Our DDR-Net achieves competitive dehazing performance with lower computational cost and fewer parameters than recent SOTA methods.
Table 1. Quantitative comparisons on real-world and synthetic dehazing benchmarks. Best results are in bold, second-best are underlined. “-” indicates unavailable results.
Fig. 2. Overall architecture of DDR-Net. (a) The encoder-decoder framework integrates SFBR at the bottleneck. (b) HPE provides complementary haze-aware representations for restoration.

Fig. 6. Evaluation on the number of DE Units. The performance exhibits an increasing trend from 1 to 4, reaching its peak values at 4 units. As the number of DE Units increases from 4 to 6, performance gradually decreases.

Fig. 3. Architectures of the Detail-Enhanced Blocks. (a) DE FusBlock splits the input features into two branches to perform refinement at multiple spatial resolutions. (b) Detailed architecture of DE ResBlock.
